claims.text: GUARD: the verb must be in ``spine.attempt.READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS`` -- the repo's own allowlist, imported so there is one list to keep right instead of two.
claims.why: The code checks `verb not in READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS` but the definition of READ_ONLY_REPO_VERBS is not in this chunk; cannot verify it is imported from spine.attempt.

claims.text: Reading history (``show``/``diff``/``rev-parse``) is exactly what this module needs from the checkout, and it needs nothing else.
claims.why: No other git verbs are used in this chunk; the claim about module's needs cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Mutating verbs are fine here and nowhere else -- which is why the cwd goes through :func:`_refuse_primary_checkout` before the process is spawned, exactly as ``spine.attempt._git`` does for its own choke point.
claims.why: The code calls _refuse_primary_checkout but that function is not defined in this chunk; cannot verify its behavior or comparison to spine.attempt._git.

claims.text: Full sha for ``rev``, or None if it does not resolve.
claims.why: The function returns None if returncode != 0, otherwise returns the stripped stdout or None if empty.

claims.text: Deliberately close to ``spine.attempt.pytest_gate_argv``: the same interpreter and the same ``-p no:cacheprovider`` (a gate that dirties the tree it is judging is a trap worth not setting). It differs in two measured ways, and both are needed for PER-NODE attribution, which ``-q`` cannot give: ``-v`` prints ``<nodeid> PASSED|FAILED|SKIPPED (reason)`` per test, which is the only output form that carries the EXACT node id for a skip -- ``-rA``'s short summary prints skips as ``SKIPPED [1] file.py:12: reason``, with no node id at all. ``--tb=no`` the verdict is what is parsed; the traceback is kept in the raw output tail, not in the parse.
claims.why: The code returns a tuple including sys.executable, -m pytest, node ids, -v, --tb=no, -p no:cacheprovider. The claim about closeness to spine.attempt.pytest_gate_argv and the behavior of -v vs -rA cannot be verified from this chunk.

claims.text: an expected failure is not a pass
claims.why: XFAIL maps to STATUS_FAILED, so expected failures are treated as failures.

claims.text: "ERROR: not found: C:\...\tests\x.py::test_y" -- the FILE collected, and the node id is not in it. The task named a test that does not exist.
claims.why: The comment describes external behavior; the regex pattern is present but its correctness in matching that specific format cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: "ERROR: found no collectors for C:\...\tests\x.py::test_y" -- a DIFFERENT fact, and conflating the two was a real defect in this parser, caught by running it: the file itself could not be collected (it imports something that does not exist on the base revision, which is the NORMAL state of a test added by the fix being evaluated). That is a test that does not pass -- a valid FAIL_TO_PASS before-state -- whereas "not found" refutes the task. Reporting the second as the first invalidated 13 of 14 nodes of a real corpus candidate.
claims.why: The comment describes historical defect and semantics; the regex patterns are present but their correct classification cannot be verified from this chunk alone.

claims.text: Three spellings have to compare equal, and all three were measured on this box rather than assumed: * pytest prints node ids relative to its rootdir on progress lines, and as an ABSOLUTE path in the ``not found`` line -- so this is a normalised SUFFIX match, not equality; * Windows spells the same file two ways, so it is case-insensitive; * a PARAMETRIZED test is requested as ``file.py::test_x`` and reported as
